Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. One word one meaning: same term for same thing every time, no synonym rotation. Instruction = imperative: "Run X", not "X should be run". Noun cluster 3 words max. 1: import { DEFAULT_SETTINGS, Settings, type ReqflowApi } from "@reqflow/core";
2: import { createStore } from "zustand/vanilla";
3: import { ReqflowError } from "./bridge-client";
4: 
5: /**
6:  * Where the settings live, as far as the UI knows:
7:  * - "loading": asking the main process
8:  * - "saved": loaded from / saved to disk
9:  * - "unavailable": main has no settings storage yet (WS1) — changes apply until the app restarts
10:  * - "error": loading or saving failed; `error` says why
11:  */
12: export type SettingsPersistence = "loading" | "saved" | "unavailable" | "error";
13: 
14: export interface SettingsState {
15:   settings: Settings;
16:   persistence: SettingsPersistence;
17:   error: string | null;
18:   /** Ask main for the stored settings. Keeps the defaults when storage isn't built yet. */
19:   load(): Promise<void>;
20:   /**
21:    * Merge `patch` into one section, validated with the `Settings` schema. Returns a readable
22:    * error and changes nothing when invalid; otherwise applies it and saves in the background.
23:    */
24:   update<K extends keyof Settings>(section: K, patch: Partial<Settings[K]>): string | null;
25:   resetSection(section: keyof Settings): void;
26: }
27: 
28: const SAVE_DELAY_MS = 400;
29: 
30: export function createSettingsStore(client: Pick<ReqflowApi, "settings">) {
31:   let saveTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
32: 
33:   return createStore<SettingsState>()((set, get) => {
34:     const save = () => {
35:       clearTimeout(saveTimer);
36:       saveTimer = setTimeout(async () => {
37:         if (get().persistence === "unavailable") return;
38:         try {
39:           const saved = await client.settings.save(get().settings);
40:           set({ settings: saved, persistence: "saved", error: null });
41:         } catch (err) {
42:           if (err instanceof ReqflowError && err.code === "not_implemented") {
43:             set({ persistence: "unavailable", error: null });
44:           } else {
45:             set({ persistence: "error", error: errorMessage(err, "Saving settings failed") });
46:           }
47:         }
48:       }, SAVE_DELAY_MS);
49:     };
50: 
51:     const apply = <K extends keyof Settings>(section: K, value: Settings[K]): string | null => {
52:       const parsed = Settings.shape[section].safeParse(value);
53:       if (!parsed.success) {
54:         const issue = parsed.error.issues[0];
55:         return issue ? issue.message : "Invalid value";
56:       }
57:       set({ settings: { ...get().settings, [section]: parsed.data } });
58:       save();
59:       return null;
60:     };
61: 
62:     return {
63:       settings: DEFAULT_SETTINGS,
64:       persistence: "loading",
65:       error: null,
66: 
67:       async load() {
68:         set({ persistence: "loading", error: null });
69:         try {
70:           const stored = Settings.parse(await client.settings.get());
71:           set({ settings: stored, persistence: "saved" });
72:         } catch (err) {
73:           if (err instanceof ReqflowError && err.code === "not_implemented") {
74:             set({ persistence: "unavailable" });
75:           } else {
76:             set({ persistence: "error", error: errorMessage(err, "Loading settings failed") });
77:           }
78:         }
79:       },
80: 
81:       update(section, patch) {
82:         return apply(section, { ...get().settings[section], ...patch });
83:       },
84: 
85:       resetSection(section) {
86:         apply(section, DEFAULT_SETTINGS[section]);
87:       },
88:     };
89:   });
90: }
91: 
92: function errorMessage(err: unknown, fallback: string): string {
93:   return err instanceof Error && err.message ? `${fallback}: ${err.message}` : fallback;
94: }

8: /** Thrown by every `api.*` call that fails in the main process. `code` is machine-readable. */
9: export class ReqflowError extends Error {
10:   constructor(
11:     readonly code: string,
12:     message: string,
13:     readonly details?: unknown,

15:     super(message);
16:     this.name = "ReqflowError";

20: type InvokeClient = {
21:   [N in keyof typeof IPC_INVOKE_METHODS]: {
22:     [M in (typeof IPC_INVOKE_METHODS)[N][number]]: M extends keyof ReqflowApi[N]
23:       ? ReqflowApi[N][M]
24:       : never;
25:   };
26: };

28: /** Builds the typed API from the bridge; a method missing from IPC_INVOKE_METHODS is a type error here. */
29: export function createApi(bridge: ReqflowBridge): ReqflowApi {
30:   const client = Object.fromEntries(
31:     Object.entries(IPC_INVOKE_METHODS).map(([ns, methods]) => [
32:       ns,
33:       Object.fromEntries(
34:         methods.map((method) => [
35:           method,
36:           async (...args: unknown[]) => {
37:             const result = await bridge.invoke(ipcChannel(ns, method), ...args);
38:             if (!result.ok) {
39:               throw new ReqflowError(result.error.code, result.error.message, result.error.details);
40:             }
41:             return result.value;
42:           },
43:         ]),
44:       ),
45:     ]),
46:   ) as InvokeClient;
47:   return { ...client, runs: { ...client.runs, onUpdate: bridge.onRunUpdate } };

1: # Workstreams — how to split the work across agents
2: 
3: Each workstream (WS) owns a set of paths, so parallel agents never edit the same files. Everything
4: builds against the contract in `packages/core` (block specs in `blocks.ts`, graph rules in `graph.ts`)
5: and the block contract in `packages/engine/src/block.ts`. UI workstreams use `@reqflow/core/fixtures`
6: until the API is live. Block workstreams test with fixtures and the `mock` LLM.
7: 
8: ## Starting an agent
9: 
10: Paste [AGENT_PROMPT.md](AGENT_PROMPT.md) into the agent, with the workstream filled in. Agents claim
11: work and hand it off in [STATUS.md](STATUS.md), each editing only its own section. **The concrete,
12: ordered task list for every workstream lives in STATUS.md**; this file defines scope, file ownership
13: and "done when".
14: 
15: ## UI agents (WS2–WS4)
16: 
17: The renderer is sandboxed: no Node, no `fs`, no `fetch` to the internet. Reach data only through
18: `api` from `@/lib/api`. Until WS1 implements a method, it throws `ReqflowError` with code
19: `not_implemented`. Show that state, or render `@reqflow/core/fixtures` meanwhile. Reuse the shared
20: controls in `components/ui/` and the design tokens in `globals.css` (light and dark). Check your
21: screens with `npm run smoke` (screenshots land in `apps/desktop/out/smoke/`), and extend
22: `apps/desktop/src/main/smoke.ts` (ask WS1/WS0) when you add an interaction worth guarding.
23: 
24: ## Git
25: 
26: Use one branch per workstream (`ws1-engine`, `ws2-editor`, …), ideally in its own `git worktree`. Make small
27: commits (`ws<N>: …`), push right away, and rebase on `main` at least hourly. Merge into `main` through a PR
28: with a merge commit, never a squash, so Entire's checkpoint trailers survive. To add a dependency, add it to **your own** package's
29: `package.json` only. If `package-lock.json` conflicts, run `npm install` again.
30: 
31: ## Phases
32: 
33: 0. **Done (lead):** repo skeleton, the contract (`core`: schemas, block specs, graph rules), the block
34:    contract and registry, the default template, fixtures, the app shell with its three tabs, the Data
35:    Flow editor (structure), the Settings page and the Car placeholder.
36: 1. **Parallel:** WS1–WS8 below.
37: 2. **Integration (lead):** wire services and the registry in `apps/desktop/src/main`, run the default template end
38:    to end with `mock`, then with Claude and the real BMW data, then polish the demo.
39: 
40: ---
41: 
42: ### WS0 — Lead / integrator (main session)
43: 
44: **Owns:** `packages/core/**`, `docs/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `PRODUCT.md`, root config files.
45: **Does:** merges branches, reviews and applies contract changes (including block params and ports), runs
46: integration (phase 2) and keeps docs current.
47: 
48: ### WS1 — Engine, persistence & main process
49: 
50: **Owns:** `packages/engine/**`, `packages/db/**`, `apps/desktop/src/main/**`, `apps/desktop/src/preload/**`,
51: `packages/blocks/src/hil/**`, `packages/blocks/src/index.ts`, `packages/blocks/src/templates/**`.
52: **Builds:**
53: 
54: - **First,** the handlers the UIs need: `settings.get/save` (the Settings page already calls them),
55:   `workflows.*` (so the editor can save and load), `files.import` (Raw's file param), and read-only
56:   `requirements.*` / `audit.list` serving the core fixtures until the DB lands.
57: - The executor (see ARCHITECTURE.md → Engine semantics): `validateGraph`, topological run per workplace,
58:   inner workplaces via boundary blocks, merge per input port, per-port output storage, failure →
59:   skipped, pause/resume at HIL, cancel. Wire `BlockContext` (including `ctx.car.add` → DB).
60: - SQLite repositories, versioned requirements, append-only `AuditLogger`, `FileStore`, settings storage.
61: - Every method in `main/handlers.ts` (replace each `notBuilt`), with Zod validation of all arguments. Wire registry, LLM, web search, DB and keychain (`safeStorage`) in `main/`; push run updates via `IPC_EVENTS.runUpdate`.
62: - The HIL block (pause until reviewed, then pass on what the reviewer kept).
63: 
64: **Done when:** executor tests pass with fake blocks (success, failure, multi-port merge, splitter
65: fan-out, inner workplace, pause → resume, cancel). Every IPC method works against SQLite (none left
66: `not_implemented`). A run of fake blocks streams updates to `runs.onUpdate`.
67: 
68: ### WS2 — Data Flow editor UI
69: 
70: **Owns:** `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/pages/DataflowPage.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/dataflow/**`.
71: **State today:** palette, workplace (React Flow), blocks with ports, connect with validation, inspector
72: with parameter forms, inner workplaces with breadcrumb, delete with confirmation, snap/minimap from
73: Settings. The flow lives in memory (`components/dataflow/store.ts`).

75: undo/redo, copy/paste, a Run button with live status, counts and logs on each block
76: (`api.runs.onUpdate()`), an output inspector (`api.runs.blockOutput()`), and a "waiting for review"
77: banner linking to the Car tab.
78: **Done when:** you can build the default template by hand, save it, reload it, and see run states on the
79: blocks (mocked until WS1 lands).
80: 
81: ### WS3 — Car tab: requirements review & audit UI
82: 
83: **Owns:** `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/pages/CarPage.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/car/**`,
84: `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/requirements/**`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/audit/**`.
85: **Builds:** the Car tab as the output page: the car (keep the car visual) with its requirements as a
86: list or board, grouped by ranking, with filters and sorting. A detail view shows targets, a score
87: breakdown (factor × weight with notes), priority and rationale, an evidence level badge, assumptions,
88: uncertainties and conflicting evidence, and a drill-down from findings to verbatim excerpts to sources.
89: Add a decision bar (approve / reject / defer / challenge) where rationale is required, inline editing
90: with rationale, a History view, a global audit timeline with before → after diffs and filters, a
91: resume-run action, and export.
92: **Done when:** every field from the briefing's deliverable list is visible for the fixture requirements,
93: and the decision and edit flows call `api.requirements.*`.
94: 
95: ### WS4 — Settings, app shell & packaging
96: 
97: **Owns:** `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/settings/**`,
98: `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/shell/**`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/ui/**` (shared controls),
99: `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/lib/settings*.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/lib/theme.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/router.tsx`,
100: `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/globals.css`, `apps/desktop/electron-builder.yml`, `apps/desktop/build/**` (app icons).
101: **State today:** bottom tab bar (⌘/Ctrl 1–3), Settings with App, Global parameters, AI & research,
102: Collaboration and About; theme switching (system/light/dark); every change validated with the
103: `Settings` schema. Not saved yet (waits for WS1's `settings.save`).
104: **Builds next:** API-key entry once `settings.setSecret` exists (never display a stored key), a
105: `settings.changed` audit entry once WS1 logs it, the app icon and installer config, demo polish.
106: **Done when:** settings load, validate, save and appear as a `settings.changed` audit event, the shell looks
107: demo-ready, and `npm run package` produces a working installer on your OS.
108: 
109: ### WS5 — Raw block (BMW data ingestion)
110: 
111: **Owns:** `packages/blocks/src/raw/**`, `data/samples/**`.
112: **Builds:** the Raw block. Params (see `BLOCK_SPECS.raw`): Excel upload (`file` = `{ fileId, name }`
113: from `api.files.import()`, `sheet`) or database (`dbType`, `connection`, `query`; never store
114: passwords in params), plus `dataset`. It parses the provided formats (CSV, XLSX and whatever BMW
115: ships: check `data/raw/` once it arrives) into `Source` + `SourceRecord[]` with locators and language.
116: Structured datasets (equipment take rates, sales volumes) also emit deterministic `usage_pattern`
117: findings (for example a high take rate signals a basic expectation) with evidence. Also write
118: synthetic sample files in `data/samples/` that match the real formats. Param changes → request via WS0.
119: **Done when:** each sample dataset ingests in tests, errors name the bad row or column, and no data is dropped silently.
120: 
121: ### WS6 — Research block
122: 
123: **Owns:** `packages/blocks/src/research/**`.
124: **Builds:** the Research block. It turns its params and the scope into queries (competitors in the
125: segment, owner and press reviews, market and technology trends for the horizon), runs them through
126: `ctx.web`, fetches pages and extracts clean text into `SourceRecord`s — the same stream format as Raw —
127: and sets the `Source` kind, publisher, date and **reliability** (with the rule documented). It respects
128: allowed and blocked domains and de-duplicates by URL. Also implement `WebSearch` providers
129: (`anthropic_web_search`, `tavily`) as factories that take keys as arguments (WS1 wires them).
130: **Done when:** a recorded or offline test run produces sources with working URLs and reliability, and failures are logged rather than swallowed.
131: 
132: ### WS7 — AI blocks: AI Filter, AI Splitter, Add to Car
133: 
134: **Owns:** `packages/llm/**`, `packages/blocks/src/ai-filter/**`, `packages/blocks/src/ai-splitter/**`,
135: `packages/blocks/src/add-to-car/**`.
136: **Builds:** an `LlmClient` with a Claude provider and a deterministic `mock` provider (use the `claude-api`
137: skill for SDK details). **AI Filter**: keep items matching the criterion and extract evidence-linked
138: findings (verbatim-excerpt verification; out-of-scope items logged with a reason). **AI Splitter**:
139: route every item to exactly one branch (`out-<i>`); "Split by: Priority" uses WS8's scoring.
140: **Add to Car**: cluster and derive customer-facing, actionable requirements (IDs from
141: `formatRequirementId`, measurable targets, evidence level per the A–D rule, Kano class, assumptions,
142: uncertainties, conflicting findings), set the priority from the input port's ranking, and hand them
143: to `ctx.car.add`. Also export `answerChallenge(...)` for the API's challenge flow.
144: **Done when:** fixture records → filter → splitter → Add to Car runs fully offline with `mock`, all
145: outputs parse against the core schemas, and every finding's excerpt is verified.
146: 
147: ### WS8 — Prioritization
148: 
149: **Owns:** `packages/blocks/src/prioritization/**`.
150: **Builds:** explainable scoring used by the AI Splitter's priority mode. Factors are computed
151: deterministically where possible: customer impact from mentions, sentiment and sales volume; evidence
152: strength from independent sources × reliability and evidence level; competitive gap from
153: `competitor_advantage` findings; trend momentum from `market_trend` findings. The LLM is used only

+# Research API Settings
+
+Open **Settings → Research APIs & Zugänge** to manage research access. This section is separate
+from the existing AI model and web-search settings. It does not start research or select a model.
+
+## Providers
+
+The nine providers are grouped into web search, social/community access, and studies/documents:
+
+| Provider | Credential fields | Additional controls |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Firecrawl | `firecrawl_api_key` | Enabled switch; explicit connection test |
+| Tavily (alternative) | `tavily_api_key` | Enabled switch; explicit connection test; does not replace the selected search provider |
+| YouTube | `youtube_api_key` | Enabled switch; explicit connection test |
+| Apify (Instagram/TikTok) | `apify_api_token` | Separate platform approval and fixed actor allowlist |
+| X | `x_bearer_token` | Recent/full-archive selector; the account plan must permit the selected mode |
+| Reddit | `reddit_client_id`, `reddit_client_secret`, `reddit_refresh_token` | Separate research approval and identifiable user-agent |
+| OpenAlex | `openalex_api_key` (optional) | Actual access and quota limitations come from the connection report |
+| Eurostat | None | Public statistics; choose datasets in the workflow |
+| Local documents | None | Uses documents imported and selected in Data Flow; no external connection |
+
+Official provider documentation links open in the system browser using the existing Electron
+external-link handler. Local documents do not have an external service or API-key setup page.
+
+Apify actor selection is limited to `APIFY_ACTORS` from the final shared contract:
+
+- `apify/instagram-scraper`
+- `apify/instagram-comment-scraper`
+- `clockworks/tiktok-scraper`
+- `clockworks/tiktok-comments-scraper`
+
+Reddit's user-agent input requires an identifiable client in the form
+`desktop:ReqFlow:0.1 (by /u/your_reddit_username)`, with 10–200 characters. Replace the example
+username with the contact for your approved client. The shared schema is also validated before
+configuration is submitted. These controls do not obtain platform permission on your behalf.
+
+## Credentials and connection reports
+
+- Inputs are masked, start empty, and never receive a configured credential from main.
+- **Save** submits only a nonempty, trimmed draft. Empty or whitespace-only input cannot delete
+  a credential. A successful save clears the draft before refreshing status, including when that
+  refresh fails.
+- **Remove** is a separate button for each configured credential. It alone submits `null` to
+  delete the saved credential. An environment credential may remain configured after removal;
+  the refreshed main status is authoritative.
+- Saving or removing a key reloads provider statuses. Neither operation enables a provider,
+  grants approval, tests a connection, nor launches collection.
+- **Enabled**, **platform approval**, **credential configured**, and **connection tested** are
+  distinct. A successful test never implies provider activation or platform approval.
+- **Test connection** is an explicit, small check. It may consume API quota or credits. It does
+  not launch a research workflow. The local-document check has no external request.
+
+The UI shows the exact `ConnectionReport.state` code, its human-readable label, the main-process
+message, `testedAt` when present, capabilities, and limitations. The supported codes are:
+`not_configured`, `untested`, `success`, `invalid_credentials`, `permission_required`,
+`rate_limited`, `unreachable`, and `unsupported`. A configured credential is not shown as a
+successful connection. Missing statuses are displayed as unavailable, never replaced with demo
+or fabricated results. Loading and error states provide an explicit status reload action.
+
+The existing **AI & research → API keys** area now accepts a masked Anthropic key in the same
+`anthropic_api_key` namespace. Saving/removing it reloads secret status without changing `llm`
+settings. The existing Tavily status points to the new Research API section for editing.
+
+## IPC boundary and persistence
+
+Renderer operations use the existing typed `api` bridge only:
+
+```ts
+api.research.providers(): Promise<ResearchProviderStatus[]>
+api.research.configure(id, config): Promise<ResearchProviderStatus>
+api.research.test(id): Promise<ResearchProviderStatus>
+api.settings.setSecret(name, valueOrNull): Promise<SecretStatus>
+```
+
+Anthropic status is read with `api.settings.secrets()`. Secrets are never included in provider
+configuration or the settings autosave store. The renderer performs no network, filesystem, or
+Node operations. Only sanitized `ReqflowError.message` strings from main are displayed for
+rejected calls; arbitrary errors, raw objects, and error details are not rendered.
+
+Configuration uses the complete validated current `ResearchProviderConfig`, preserving fields
+not edited by the control. After `configure` succeeds, the UI awaits the existing
+`settingsStore.getState().load()` method so later settings autosaves use the persisted
+`settings.research.apis` object. This reload is performed even if the section was unmounted
+while configuring. A failed store reload is reported as an action failure rather than hidden.
+
+Research operations are serialized within the section. Inputs and action buttons are disabled
+while an operation is pending. Generation guards discard stale responses after unmount or effect
+replay, and credential drafts are discarded on unmount. Anthropic has an independent pending guard
+and request generation. These guards do not cancel an IPC write that main has already received.
+
+### Main-process assumptions
+
+- `configure` persists `settings.research.apis[id]` in the same Settings object returned by
+  `settings.get`, and returns one status rather than a list.
+- `test` returns one status, does not activate a provider or grant approval, and returns sanitized
+  report messages/capabilities/limitations.
+- Provider statuses identify configured credentials by the exact `SecretName` keys listed above.
+- Credential changes invalidate or otherwise accurately update any previous connection report;
+  `providers()` must not return an old success as a test of the new credential.
+- `setSecret(name, null)` removes the saved credential; environment fallback may remain.
+- The current settings store has no flush/cancellation method for an already-running full-settings
+  autosave. The reload protects subsequent saves, not a write already in flight. Main/store owners
+  must coordinate concurrent full-settings writes if this case is supported.
+
+## Focused verification
+
+No live provider checks or real credentials are used by the tests.
+
+```sh
+npm exec -- vitest run apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/settings/sections/ResearchApisSection.test.ts
+npm run typecheck
+npm test
+npm run smoke
+```
+
+Controller tests cover all provider/credential mappings, report codes, blank-save safety,
+explicit removal, draft clearing, failed status refresh, sanitized errors, preservation of
+configuration, fixed actor validation, separate testing/approval/enablement, pending guards,
+and stale/unmounted responses. Static rendering tests use existing React DOM support; no new
+test package is required.
+
+The existing smoke script does not yet visit `settings-section-research-apis`. Its owner can
+add that ID to `SETTINGS_SECTIONS` to capture the new section in future smoke runs. Do not run
+live connection tests as part of smoke.
